planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant outdoors once nights stay reliably above 55°F.

directions: Ruby King is an American heirloom sweet bell pepper documented since at least 1902 and preserved through the Seed Savers Exchange network after a 1977 donation. It sets heavy clusters of blocky, thick-walled fruit that ripen from green to a deep glossy red, with a mild, sweet flavor that holds up well fresh or cooked. Give plants full sun and consistent moisture, and stake or cage heavily loaded branches since the large fruit can weigh down stems. Its earlier maturity than many modern giant bells makes it a reliable choice for gardeners in shorter-season regions.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and set transplants out once the soil has warmed and frost danger has passed.

directions: World Beater, also sold as Ruby Giant, is a pre-1912 heirloom sweet pepper bred from a cross of Chinese Giant and Ruby King, combining the size of one parent with the productivity of the other. Fruits are exceptionally large and blocky with thick, sweet flesh that ripens from green to red, making it a favorite for stuffing or roasting whole. The sturdy, three-foot plants carry a heavy fruit load, so working in compost at planting and providing steady, even moisture helps size the peppers properly. Choose this variety when garden space allows for a true old-fashioned giant bell rather than a modern hybrid.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, since chinense types germinate slowly and need sustained bottom heat; transplant only after the soil is thoroughly warm.

directions: Zavory was bred to deliver the full fruity, floral aroma of a habanero with almost none of the heat, registering only around 100 Scoville units compared to 30,000 or more for a standard habanero. Glossy, bullet-shaped fruit ripens through green, yellow, orange, and finally red on prolific, heat-loving plants, and any single stage can be harvested for eating. Because it needs a long, warm season to size up and ripen fully, start seed early indoors and grow it in the hottest, sunniest spot available. It suits cooks who want habanero flavor in salsas, chutneys, or fresh salads without the burn.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, providing bottom heat for slow-to-germinate chinense seed, and transplant once nights stay warm.

directions: NuMex Suave Red was released by the Chile Pepper Institute at New Mexico State University as a nearly heatless habanero, measuring only a few hundred Scoville units yet retaining the same fruity, tropical aroma prized in hot habaneros. Plump, wrinkled fruit ripens from green to a deep red on productive plants that need a long, warm season to reach full size. Because the pepper carries little to no burn, it lets cooks use habanero flavor generously in salsas and sauces without overwhelming heat. Give it the same rich soil, consistent watering, and full sun that other chinense peppers require to perform well.
sources: New Mexico State University Chile Pepper Institute
New Mexico State University Cooperative Extension

planting.note: Start seed indoors about 8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm soil after danger of frost has passed.

directions: Merlot is an early, compact F1 sweet bell hybrid grown for its unusual color sequence, shifting from green to white before purple stripes spread and merge into a deep wine-purple fruit that finishes red if left on the plant. Its short, sturdy habit and disease tolerance make it dependable in both cool springs and hot, humid summers, and the thick walls hold up well for stuffing or fresh slicing. Choose it for a striking, out-of-the-ordinary bell pepper color in mixed vegetable and ornamental edible plantings. Regular harvesting at the purple stage encourages continued fruit set through the season.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm soil after all frost danger has passed.

directions: Blushing Beauty was named an All-America Selections winner for a fruit that skips green entirely, opening ivory and then blushing through light pink, orange-red, and finally deep scarlet as it ripens, often showing several colors on the plant at once. The thick-walled, blocky fruit is sweet and usable at any color stage, giving gardeners flexibility in when to harvest. Its compact, disease-resistant plants perform well in containers on a patio as well as in a garden bed, and the multicolored fruit display makes it as ornamental as it is productive. Pick some fruit at the pale stage to encourage continued setting through the season.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant outdoors once the soil has warmed and frost danger has passed.

directions: Ozark Giant is an old regional heirloom prized for producing some of the largest bell peppers a home gardener can grow, with fruit commonly reaching six inches or more in length on sturdy, heavy-bearing plants. The thick, crisp flesh ripens from green to red and is noted for a flavor considered sweeter and more robust than many modern bell hybrids. Because the plants carry an unusually heavy fruit load for their size, staking helps prevent branches from snapping once peppers begin to size up. It performs especially well through hot, humid Southern summers, making it a strong choice for gardeners in the region where it originated.
